questions.question: A shop marks up its goods by 50 percent on cost. (a) Calculate the selling price of an item costing R600. (b) Calculate the cost of an item sold for R1 200. (c) Explain why taking 50 percent off R1 200 is incorrect.
questions.expected_answer: (a) 600 + 600 × 50 percent = 600 + 300 = R900. (b) 1 200 × 100 ÷ 150 = R800. (c) The mark-up is calculated on cost, so the selling price is 150 percent of cost; taking 50 percent off the selling price gives R600, and 600 plus 50 percent is only R900, not R1 200.

questions.question: Show the effect on the accounting equation of a cash sale of goods costing R600 for R900.
questions.expected_answer: Sales part: Assets +900 (Bank, money received); OE +900 (income: sales). Cost part: Assets -600 (Trading stock, stock sold); OE -600 (expense: cost of sales). Net: A +300; OE +300 (gross profit); L 0.

questions.question: Name the source document for each: (a) total cash sales for the day; (b) rent income received; (c) wages paid by EFT.
questions.expected_answer: (a) Cash register roll (CRR). (b) Duplicate receipt. (c) EFT payment confirmation (proof of payment) or the bank statement.
